answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a public contract before it can submit work, and the bond is slashed when independent reviewers prove fraud under a stated rule. A fake-identity attacker can still create many accounts, but each one requires more capital at risk; splitting a fixed budget across identities also makes each bond smaller and less credible. The cipher audit records claims, while jade and zephyr label two reviewer samples, not magical defenses: the deterrent is the enforceable, per-identity cost.
